opening.argument: The interaction is framed as a security-research test of a purported technical-support scam, not as an offer made by the video. The caller expressly states, “I actually am a security researcher and I was testing various TechSupport scams,” then explains that he wanted to determine whether the scam also worked on a Mac and report the result. The representative’s directions toward a remote-support connection, TeamViewer credentials, and paid support are presented as evidence gathered during that investigation. The caller also directly challenges the technical explanation and asks whether the interaction is a scam, reinforcing that the exchange is being examined critically rather than promoted. The $200 support plan and payment page therefore function as subjects of the test, while the caller’s questioning establishes the investigative context.
